wrong-inverse-operation: Use the opposite operation to move a term: subtract to undo addition, add to undo subtraction, divide to undo multiplication.
forgot-divide-by-coefficient: After you isolate the x-term you still have to divide both sides by the number multiplying x.
arithmetic-error: Your method was right — check the arithmetic.
ignored-left-side: Whatever you do to the right side you must also do to the left side.
ignored-right-side: Simplify the right side too — gather the x terms on one side and the numbers on the other.
ignored-constant: Deal with the plain number term first by adding or subtracting it from both sides.
ignored-parentheses: Start by distributing the outside number over every term inside the brackets.
distributed-incorrectly: When distributing, multiply the outside number by every term inside the brackets.
partially-distributed: Distribute to all terms inside the brackets, not just the first one.
combined-constants-incorrectly: Combine the plain number terms carefully — subtract a negative means you add.
combined-like-terms-incorrectly: Only combine terms with the same variable. Subtract the coefficients, not the letters.
wrong-operation-order: Undo addition or subtraction first, then undo multiplication or division.
misread-problem: Translate the words into an equation first — decide what x stands for, then build the equation.
divided-instead-of-multiplied: When x is being divided, multiply both sides to undo it.
added-instead-of-subtracted: Check the sign: a minus on one side becomes adding when you move it across.
subtracted-instead-of-added: To undo subtraction, add the same amount to both sides.
added-coefficients-incorrectly: When you move a variable term across, its sign flips.
ignored-variables-side: Group the x terms on one side before you solve.
halved-incorrectly: Halve both sides, not just one.
multiplied-by-wrong-number: Multiply by the number x is being divided by.
forgot-multiply-both-sides: Multiply every term on both sides, not just the x term.
forgot-add-constant: Don't forget the constant term still needs to be moved across.
divided-before-subtracting: Do the addition or subtraction step first, then the division.
